claude.rationale: gap_45=1: Kingfisher's customer-facing midstream product (pipelines, cryogenic processing plant, gathering/processing/marketing) crossed the ownership boundary, but Kingfisher "has no employees" and its operating/delivery processes were performed by third-party operator ARM under an Operator Agreement that was "terminate[d] effective upon the Closing" — so the delivering process did not transfer whole with the asset. gap_56=1: the operational processes were not run by an internalized workforce; the Operator Agreement terminated and continuity was bridged not by a people/organization transfer but externally. gap_mitigated=yes: at Closing Kingfisher entered a six-month operating "Transition Services Agreement" with ARM under which ARM "will provide certain operational services," contractually absorbing the process/people substrate at closing. (Alta Mesa's executive team and pre-existing employment agreements did continue, but the Kingfisher leg drives the structural product-vs-process and process-vs-organization mismatch.)

gemini.rationale: The transaction transferred Kingfisher's midstream assets and operational processes (T5) without an accompanying internalized workforce (T6), as Kingfisher had no employees and its pre-existing Operator Agreement was terminated at closing. This structural gap between process and organization was explicitly mitigated at closing via a six-month Transition Services Agreement with the former operator.

openai.rationale: Alta Mesa’s and Kingfisher’s customer-facing businesses and assets moved into SRII Opco, but Kingfisher’s Operator Agreement with ARM was terminated at Closing, so its operational substrate did not transfer with the assets; instead, ARM provided specified services under a six-month Transition Services Agreement. Kingfisher had no employees, and the ARM personnel who operated and managed it were not internalized, documenting a process-to-organization mismatch at Closing. The Transition Services Agreement contractually bridged both mismatches for the stated six-month period.
